implementation_contract.load_queue: A registered nonempty payload with PROCESSED_FL=FALSE and DELETED_FL=FALSE
implementation_contract.accepted_history: Batch registration remains evidence of earlier acceptance after processing or purging; do not automatically requeue historical files
implementation_contract.file_identity: Match exact physical file name and source, and normalize table qualification within KUMO_DEV; do not use filename-prefix joins
implementation_contract.empty_files: Validate empty payloads normally, record successful delivery acceptance in existing readiness history, and exclude them from the dbt queue
implementation_contract.historical_empty_files: Preserve existing source/package watermarks. Readiness history is currently empty, so do not infer historical acceptance from batch-control absence or reset watermarks during cutover
implementation_contract.delivery_completion: Require every expected payload to be accepted; a MAX/any-file test cannot establish delivery completion
implementation_contract.control_files: Validate and archive controls using the exact accepted delivery/file set. Delete only controls successfully archived for that set
implementation_contract.validation_rules: Preserve receipt, row-count, source-completeness, sequence, override and earlier-failure blocking rules
implementation_contract.reruns: Use insert-only registration for ordinary validation; leave existing batch IDs, timestamps and processing flags intact
implementation_contract.explicit_reload: Define and implement a reset for the exact reloaded file set; coordinate it with existing SDL rebuild behavior and do not reset unrelated batches
implementation_contract.atomicity: Publish successful readiness logs, batch registration, control archival and sequence advancement consistently; success must not remain visible after a later registration/archive failure
implementation_contract.compatibility: Retain derived DW_READY_TO_LOAD_FL in monitor metadata/API and existing procedure signatures; remove physical RAW reads and writes of both dropped columns
